en: The Tamaraw, the national mammal, stands only about 1 meter tall at the shoulders, making it much smaller than the domestic water buffalo.
The Philippines is administratively divided into 81 provinces grouped into 17 regions, including the highly urbanized National Capital Region.
The Philippine flag features a sun with eight rays, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule in 1896.
The Philippine Congress consists of two chambers: a Senate with exactly 24 members and a House of Representatives with over 300 members.
National hero Jose Rizal was executed by firing squad at the age of 35 on December 30, 1896, in Bagumbayan, Manila.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu features over 100 competing dance contingents, drawing more than 2 million local and international tourists annually.
The Lumad people in Mindanao comprise 18 distinct indigenous ethnolinguistic groups, with the Manobo being the largest group numbering over 300,000 individuals.
The Narra, designated as the national tree, can grow up to 30 meters tall and yields highly durable, reddish-brown hardwood.
Dr. Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines in 1957, which now operates with over 500 beds.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution contains 18 articles, including Article III, which guarantees 22 specific sections of the Bill of Rights for citizens.
The Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex spans 62 hectares of land along Manila Bay and houses multiple major performing arts theaters.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao over 2,000 years ago, climbing up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
